SiteTopo 3D – quick guide

  1. Site – search an address, PID, title (e.g. 133100/1), lat, lon or E N (MGA2020 zone 55). The LIST parcel is loaded as the subject boundary. Use “Draw boundary” for lots not yet in the cadastre.
  2. Offline data – “Link data folder…” (step 1) points the tool at the folder filled by Download Tasmanian data.bat: the MRT statewide 2 m DEM and the LIST parcels, address points, contours and landslide planning map. Chrome / Edge remember the folder; each session asks once to allow access. The 2 m DEM is read straight from the folder (only the site’s window); the LIST layers are used when the LIST website cannot be reached, or always if you choose “First”. Without the folder the 2 m DEM is streamed from the internet. Saved projects keep the site’s photo, elevation grid, boundaries and landslip map, so they reopen without internet.
  3. Field data – drop CSV/TXT, Moasure CSV/DXF, GPX/KML or GeoJSON, or paste from Excel. Columns are detected automatically; check them on the data card. Local X/Y data (e.g. Moasure) need placing: pick the origin on the map and set the rotation, or use “Place by two known points”.
  4. Transects – chainage/RL tables. Lines named A–D are placed by default through the middle of the lot with chainage 0 where the line enters the boundary: A W→E, B N→S, C NW→SE, D NE→SW. Adjust the start, bearing or chainage at start if your line differs, or click “Pick start & direction on map”. One spreadsheet holding several lines (a Line/Transect column with A, B, C…) is split automatically.
  5. Levels – per dataset choose: as recorded (AHD), fit to the background surface (least-squares offset, optionally using only points outside the boundary), tie to a benchmark (point = known RL) or a manual offset.
  6. Surface – the background DEM (MRT 2 m DEM, GA 5 m LiDAR, LIST contours, AWS SRTM tiles or your own DEM) is corrected by your data: inside the data area the surface honours your levels exactly; the correction fades to zero over the blend distance. GPS-grade sets can be smoothed instead.
  7. Landslip & sections – step 6 loads the LIST Landslide Planning Map (hazard bands + MRT components), reports what intersects the lot and exports a landslip sheet. Add test holes (Hole, E, N, From, To, Unit) to build layered sections along the transects or your own lines; export DXF (Slide2 / SLOPE/W), CSV and a section sheet.
  8. Simulations – step 7 runs screening models on the merged surface: infinite-slope factor of safety (mean, lower bound and Monte Carlo probability of FoS < 1, as SAGA SAFETYFACTOR), SHALSTAB critical rainfall (as GRASS r.shalstab), GPP random-walk run-out (as SAGA sim_geomorphology) and an indicative single-phase Voellmy mass flow (like r.avaflow), animated in 3D and exportable as a video (MP4 in Chrome / Edge). Draw release areas, or use cells with FoS < 1 or the LIST source areas. “Export run package” writes the DEM, release and soil-depth grids with ready-to-run run_saga.bat / run_grass.bat scripts and r.avaflow inputs; drop their GeoTIFF / ASC results back on step 7 to show them in 3D and on the sheet.
  9. Outputs – 3D PNG at up to 4800 px, and a scaled 2D plan (A4/A3, 300 dpi) with contours over the aerial photo. PNGs carry their DPI so they insert at the right size in Word.

Background contours are indicative and only as good as the source DEM. Check field datum ties before relying on absolute levels.
